data.name: Seinarukana -The Spirit of Eternity Sword 2-
data.detailed_description:
Story

A journey across infinite worlds.

The Time Tree. Countless branches extending through space, each a world of its own.

In one such world, a boy holds within him the soul of an ancient god yearning to break free. He tries to live a normal life, but must constantly struggle against the destructive urges threatening to overwhelm him. Little does he know that his closest friends also carry the burdens of an age long forgotten. With this destiny comes power; Eternity Swords with incredible might and Guardian Spirits manifested from their very souls.

The gods are reborn, friend turns on friend, and an ancient war erupts once more. Thrown into a world not his own, Nozomu must fight to bring his friends home. He must also discover the true nature of the being within him before it consumes him utterly. Thus begins a journey that will shake the very foundation of the universe.

Features

  • An epic fantasy story that spans an infinite multiverse.
  • Over 50 Hours of tactical RPG game-play.
  • Six unique endings to unlock.
  • Three difficulty levels to test your skill.
  • Deep combat that challenges you to find the right path to victory.
  • Build an army from 19 playable characters with hundreds of diverse skills.
  • Conquer over 100 strongholds and build powerful Artifacts to aid you in battle.

reviews.review:
Next installment of Spirit of Eternity Sword virtual novels/SRPG. I was pretty OK with previous story (Aselia), but much less so with Seinarukana. 

I felt Aselia story much more mature and nuanced - characters had development, MC needed to fight for his girl, some heavy themes were included and the endings were quite bittersweet. This is how I liked stories of coming to age (long, long ago ;) ). All characters show real character development (and not always for better). The weakest point was MC being quite moronic for most part (but in later chapters developms as well), but this is common theme in VN. 

Seinarukana does things opposite. Characters are quite bland, behave childishly and do not develop much. And often for worse (looking at you, Nozomi and Narukana). Girls are falling over themsleves for MC for no obvious reasons and with no effort on his part. There is not much depth in the writing and it very often defies logic (no, we have no time for quick coup the grace of boss we defeated for 3rd time. We need time to discuss our feelings and that we really need to continue fight the monsters all around us...). No sacrificies, all endings are super happy endings and most of them in really stupid way. There were some redeeming qualities (MC is not so moronic than in Aselia), but I would go with "No" recommendation if based on VN. This is all age version - but I do not think story will be helped by h scenes.

On the other hand battle system got more nuanced and gives more strategic options. Apart from recycling maps (which I really despise) I anjoyed strategy game more. 

i kind of enjoyed the game and pushed myself to finish it, so I will give thumb up - but very marginally. Go play Aselia instead if you had not.
